qwen.ref_text: On the battlefield, four players with monster-like strength appeared. Each of the players had already destroyed their colonies. These players were so equally strong, they created a four-way deadlock.

lines: Algorithms, phase five. Convex hulls. This is how computers find the outline of a crowd.
Imagine seven pins, with a rubber band stretched round every one.
Stretch a rubber band round every pin.
Let go, and the band snaps onto the outer pins.
Let go. It snaps onto the outer pins.
The pins it touches are the corners of the convex hull.
The pins it touches are the hull corners.
A dent lets a segment poke outside the shape.
A dent lets a segment poke outside.
In a convex shape, every segment between two points stays inside.
A convex shape keeps every segment inside.
Walk from P to A to B, and see which way you turn.
Walk from p to a to b. Left or right?
Multiply across and subtract. A positive answer means a left turn.
Multiply across, subtract: positive means left.
Now try a different path.
Now try a different path.
This time the answer is negative, and that means a right turn.
Negative means a right turn.
And one more path.
And one more path.
Here the answer is zero, which means a straight line.
Zero means a straight line.
Now walk round the hull, one corner at a time.
Walk round the hull, corner by corner.
Going anticlockwise, every turn is a left turn.
Anticlockwise, every turn is a left turn.
If we go through F instead, we turn right.
Go through F and you turn right.
A right turn means a dent, not a corner.
Right turn: a dent, not a corner.
A computer has no rubber band. So way one is to wrap.
A computer has no rubber band. Way one: wrap.
The leftmost point must be on the hull, so we start there.
The leftmost point must be on the hull.
Now swing a line clockwise from a point r above A.
Swing a line clockwise from r.
Every point the line touches gets an angle.
Every point it touches gets an angle.
The smallest angle wins, so the first edge runs from A to G.
Smallest angle wins: A to G.
Repeat from G, starting the swing along the last edge.
Repeat from G. Start the swing along the last edge.
Each round, the first point touched is the next corner.
Each round, the first point touched is the next corner.
Back at A. That is one sweep per corner, five in all.
Back at A. One sweep per corner: 5 sweeps.
Way two is to sort the points first.
Way two: sort the points first.
The lowest point must be on the hull.
The lowest point must be on the hull.
Sort the other points by angle, sweeping anticlockwise.
Sort the rest by angle, sweeping anticlockwise.
Now walk the points in that order.
Walk the points in this order.
The path still has dents, at F and B.
The path still has dents.
Start the stack with C and D.
Start the stack with C and D.
A left turn keeps the middle point.
Left turn: keep the middle point.
A right turn means a dent, so we pop it.
A right turn is a dent: pop it.
Another left turn, so we push B.
Left turn again: push B.
A right turn again. Pop B, then push A.
A right turn again: pop B, then push A.
The stack is now the hull. It took one pass after the sort.
The stack is the hull. One pass after the sort.
Take one thousand and twenty-four points, with only four corners.
1,024 points, and only 4 are corners.
One sweep checks every point.
One sweep checks all 1,024 points.
Four corners means four sweeps, so four thousand and ninety-six steps.
4 corners, 4 sweeps: 4,096 steps.
A sort halves the list again and again.
A sort halves the list again and again.
That makes ten halvings, since two to the power ten is one thousand and twenty-four.
Ten halvings: log₂ 1,024 = 10.
So the sort makes ten passes, about ten thousand two hundred and forty steps.
The sort makes 10 passes: about 10,240 steps.
With few corners, wrapping wins.
Few corners: wrapping wins.
Now make every point a corner.
Now every point is a corner.
At ten corners they tie. Beyond that, wrapping loses.
At 10 corners they tie. More, and wrapping loses.
Now the scan wins, and wrapping costs about one hundred times more.
Scan wins. Wrapping costs about 100 times more.
Try every pair of the seven points, and there are twenty-one.
Try every pair: 21 of them.
The farthest pair is A and E, and both are corners.
The farthest pair is A and E: two corners.
An inside point always loses to a corner.
An inside point always loses to a corner.
So we drop every pair that uses an inside point.
So drop every pair that uses an inside point.
Now take one thousand points, with ten corners.
1,000 points, 10 corners.
That leaves forty-five pairs to check, instead of nearly half a million.
45 pairs to check, not 499,500.
One cross product tells left from right.
Wrapping swings a line, and costs n times h.
Scanning sorts first, then pops the dents, and costs n log n.
With few corners, wrap. With many corners, scan.
